Until now, you ran every command yourself, on your laptop, when you wanted. A real data team cannot work like that. Dashboards are read every morning by people who never open dbt; they need production tables that are built on time, tested, and never broken by a half-finished change. Ten analytics engineers change the same project every day; each change must be checked automatically before it reaches production.
This chapter puts the pieces together:
(where code runs: your development schema, a CI schema, production),
(who runs dbt, when, with which commands) and

(every pull request is built and tested automatically, and what is merged is deployed). You will see how the dbt platform does it with buttons, then build the same thing yourself with dbt Core and GitHub Actions, and run it locally to prove that it works. On the exam, these topics appear as scenarios: "a developer wants to test a fix before merging", "where should unit tests run?", "why is the CI job building nothing?".

The same dbt code runs in several environments (development, CI, production) that differ only by their target: connection, schema, credentials and the Git branch they use. Changes travel from a feature branch to production through a pull request whose CI job builds only the modified models in a temporary schema, deferring the rest to production, and blocks the merge if anything fails. Production jobs run on a schedule or on events (merge, another job, API), and each kind of test has its place: unit tests in development and CI, data tests everywhere, source freshness in production.

A restaurant has a test kitchen, a tasting table and the dining room. A cook invents a new dish in the test kitchen (development). Before the dish goes on the menu, the chef tastes it at the tasting table, with the real sauces of the restaurant (CI). Only then is it served in the dining room, every day at the same time (production). Same recipes, three places, three purposes.

title: CI for dbt Core with GitHub Actions
steps.titleText: CI for dbt Core with GitHub Actions

blocks.text:
# Slim CI for dbt Core + DuckDB.
# On every pull request to main:
#   1. build a fresh database with the raw data,
#   2. build PRODUCTION from the main branch to get its manifest (the state),
#   3. build only the models changed by the pull request (and their children)
#      in the schema dbt_ci, deferring every other ref to production.
name: dbt CI

on:
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]

jobs:
  slim-ci:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    env:
      DBT_PROFILES_DIR: ${{ github.workspace }}/ci
      DBT_DUCKDB_PATH: ${{ github.workspace }}/ci_db/practice.duckdb
      DBT_USE_COLORS: "false"
    steps:
      - name: Check out the pull request (with the history, to find main)
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Set up Python
        uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: "3.12"

      - name: Install dbt
        run: pip install "dbt-core~=1.11.0" "dbt-duckdb~=1.11.0" "duckdb==1.5.6" pandas

      - name: Load the raw data into a fresh DuckDB file
        run: python ci/load_raw.py "$DBT_DUCKDB_PATH"

      - name: Build production from main (state to compare with)
        run: |
          git worktree add ../main origin/main
          cd ../main
          dbt deps
          dbt build --target prod --exclude-resource-type unit_test
          mkdir -p "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/prod-artifacts"
          cp target/manifest.json "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/prod-artifacts/"

      - name: Install packages
        run: dbt deps

      - name: List what the pull request changed
        run: dbt ls --select state:modified+ --state prod-artifacts --target ci

      # Unit tests read the columns of their inputs from the database. For a model that
      # production does not have yet (a NEW incremental model whose unit test mocks `this`),
      # there is nothing to defer to: create every changed relation first, empty.
      - name: Create the changed relations, empty
        run: dbt run --select state:modified+ --defer --state prod-artifacts --target ci --empty

      - name: Build and test the changes (unit tests, models, data tests)
        run: dbt build --select state:modified+ --defer --state prod-artifacts --target ci

"""Create a fresh practice database for CI from ci/raw/setup.sql.

    python ci/load_raw.py <path/to/practice.duckdb>

Same statements as `duckdb practice.duckdb < setup.sql`, for machines without
the DuckDB CLI (like a GitHub Actions runner). Keep the file name practice.duckdb:
DuckDB uses the file name as the database name.
"""
import os
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import duckdb

db = Path(sys.argv[1]).resolve()
raw = Path(__file__).resolve().parent / "raw"
db.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
con = duckdb.connect(str(db))
os.chdir(raw)                      # setup.sql reads data/*.csv relative to its folder
for statement in duckdb.extract_statements((raw / "setup.sql").read_text()):
    con.execute(statement)
con.close()
print(f"raw data loaded into {db}")

With dbt Core you need an orchestrator to run this: cron on a server, Airflow, Dagster, or GitHub Actions itself. A sketch of a scheduled workflow (it is
part of the practice project: our DuckDB file lives on your laptop, so a GitHub machine could not update it):

blocks.text:
name: dbt production
on:
  schedule:
    - cron: "0 5 * * *"        # every day at 05:00 UTC
  workflow_dispatch:            # plus a "Run workflow" button
jobs:
  nightly:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: "3.12"
      - run: pip install "dbt-core~=1.11.0" "dbt-snowflake~=1.11.0"
      - run: dbt deps
      - run: dbt source freshness
      - run: dbt build --target prod --exclude-resource-type unit_test
      - run: dbt docs generate --target prod
      - name: Keep the artifacts (state for CI, retry, docs)
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: prod-artifacts
          path: target/*.json
